WHAT MATTERS ON THE FARM

Every load.
Every litre.
Every working hour.

The right conversation starts with the job your machine needs to do. We assess the exact model, engine and ECU before recommending any changes.

01 / PULLING POWER

Useful torque under load

The aim is stronger, more manageable power delivery through the working range. For suitable machines, discuss response when pulling an implement, handling changing ground conditions or working through a demanding crop.

POWER MATCHED TO THE TASK

02 / FUEL EFFICIENCY

Focus on the cost of the job

Explore whether a suitable calibration can improve fuel efficiency in your actual operation. Measure fuel against work completed: litres per hectare or tonne, alongside operating hours.

Using additional power can increase hourly fuel consumption. A lower fuel bill is an objective to evaluate, never a promised percentage.

03 / PRODUCTIVITY

Make working time count

When planting and harvesting windows are tight, consistent performance matters. The goal is useful output within the machine’s capabilities, with progress measured by work completed and time taken.

MEASURE THE DIFFERENCE

Judge the result
in the field.

Agree on a baseline before making changes. Compare similar tasks and conditions so that the result reflects useful work.

Fuel requirements vary with the operation, soil and machine setup. Good maintenance and appropriate ballast remain part of an efficient operation. Read Iowa State University’s field-operation fuel guidance.

Litres per hectare
Record the fuel used and area covered during comparable fieldwork.
Litres per tonne
Compare fuel against harvested or handled output where appropriate.
Output per hour
Track hectares or tonnes completed together with operating time and work quality.
Like-for-like conditions
Keep the implement, depth, crop or soil conditions and operator approach as consistent as practical.

A MACHINE-SPECIFIC APPROACH

Start with the machine.
Set a clear goal.

A calibration is one part of the complete setup. Existing faults, wear, cooling concerns or unsuitable implements need attention before additional performance is considered.

01

Identify the platform

Share the make, model, year, engine, transmission and operating hours. ECU identification may be needed to establish software access and compatibility.

02

Explain the workload

Describe the task, implement and response you want to improve, together with current fuel use, faults and any previous tuning.

03

Agree on the scope

Confirm suitability, the proposed work, price and arrangements before booking. Set realistic expectations and discuss how to compare the result.

AGRI TUNING QUESTIONS

Know before
you book.

Can you tune every tractor or harvester?

No. Support depends on the exact model, engine, ECU and software version. Send the machine details so we can check compatibility before recommending work.

How much power or fuel saving can I expect?

There is no universal figure. Machine condition, workload and operating conditions influence the outcome. Any expected change must be discussed for your specific application; fuel savings and productivity increases are not guaranteed.

Can tuning replace a larger machine?

It does not change the machine’s rated capacities or make its transmission, axles, brakes, cooling system or implements larger. We discuss whether calibration suits the existing machine and job.

What about warranty or manufacturer support?

We are independent of the equipment manufacturers. Before proceeding, ask your warranty provider how an aftermarket calibration would affect your particular cover and support arrangements.

What should I send with my enquiry?

Include the make, exact model, year, engine, transmission, operating hours and location. Describe the main task, implement, current concerns and any previous software changes. If an engine or transmission detail is unknown, say so.
